coordinates.object_orientation: Long axis X; anterior -X, posterior +X; dorsal +Z, ventral -Z. Left lateral side faces -Y (front). Rest lowest point at Z0. D1 matches front with anterior image-left. D3 matches top after rotation only, not mirror.

view_roles.side: posterior end-on, compression and continuous fossil body
view_roles.perspective: combined lateral, dorsal and posterior profile

concept.reason: Three real views of the same selected specimen plus description resolve primary geometry. No extra concept image, and no denied image operation is retried.

representation: fossil-specimen: internal mould of conjoined shell, not restored hollow living shell
original_scope: Deep curved laterally compressed shell with offset dorsal umbo. Use real preserved internal-mould morphology; do not turn pegma impression into an exterior horn.

reference_anchor.source: Polechová 2015, Estonian Journal of Earth Sciences 64(1):84–90, doi:10.3176/earth.2015.15
reference_anchor.specimen: NM L 7852, Ribeiria apusoides, Prague, Zahořany Formation, lower Katian
reference_anchor.images: Figure 1 D1 left lateral, D2 right lateral, D3 dorsal. Use only D for primary proportions. A/C are R. johni and must not be blended; F is another R. apusoides specimen and must not donate damaged geometry.
reference_anchor.secondary: Ribeiro et al. 2022, type species R. pholadiformis: taxonomy context only; do not combine its dimensions or shape with NM L 7852.

scale.basis: Approximate image measurement using published D1 x2.1, D2 x2.2, D3 x4 magnifications and PDF A4 size 595x842pt. At rendered 1800px page height, D1 length ~294px gives23.1mm; D2 ~302px gives22.8mm; D3 ~498px gives20.7mm. Differences from orientation/print layout retained as uncertainty, not averaged into false accuracy. D3 width ~157px gives6.5mm; D1 height ~180px gives14.1mm. Rounded working model22x13x6.5mm.
scale.tolerance: 15% overall approximate display scale; no direct specimen measurement. Width/length ~0.30 and height/length ~0.59.

morphology: One laterally compressed, elongated ovate mineralized body with a deeply arcuate ventral margin and gently concave dorsal saddle. No two detached bivalve plates or hinge teeth.

Prosogyral umbo is offset toward anterior, not central and not a terminal straight spike. D1 anterior is image-left; D2 anterior image-right. Keep broad body extending posteriorly from umbonal region.

D1/D2 show a conspicuous oblique narrow cleft near the anterior dorsal area caused by the internal pegma. It is a recessed groove/slot in the mineral mould, not an exterior plate or a shell horn. Preserve blunt surviving material at its edge, no invented sharp rostrum.

D3 shows narrow lenticular cross-section, greatest fullness anterior-to-middle, tapering toward posterior. Integrate the dorsal umbonal region and cleft, rather than extruding a flat lateral silhouette at uniform thickness.
Allow subtle irregular stone relief and subdued growth traces. Large random cracks, drilled pores, deep hollow aperture and matrix slab are not required. Avoid copying fractures as generic anatomy.
This is a solid fossil internal mould, not an intact shell surface: no shiny nacre, fleshy foot, reconstructed organs, shell opening tunnel or articulated living valves.
uncertainty: Internal mould does not preserve shell thickness or pristine exterior. The original genus-level fossil-specimen proposal is retained, but represented as documented internal mould; not a full biological shell reconstruction.
Fine muscle scars and pegma depth are not metrically resolved. Bound cleft depth from D views and keep it anatomically local; do not invent through-holes.
Approximate scale comes from print magnifications, not caliper measurements; no millimetre-accurate replica claim.
Do not overstate the original adjective strongly offset: use actual specimen umbo position and curvature, without artificial exaggeration.
palette: Matte warm-grey fossil stone, one principal material; artistic presentation, not original biological colour.
acceptance_focus: Front lateral view must show deep curved belly, dorsal concavity, anteriorly offset umbonal region and localized pegma cleft.
Side end view and top dorsal view must expose lateral compression and tapered lenticular thickness; not a flat cutout.
Perspective must show the same continuous mineralized body and cleft, without a detached horn or invented hollow shell.
Four standard views; independent QA must verify the internal-mould scope matches the original fossil-specimen target. Prep is not scientific PASS.
